trans-unit.source: Paul replied that he knew the law prohibited people from speaking evil about the ruler of the people.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~5#Answer:What did Paul reply?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~5#Answer:What did Paul reply?487791685
trans-unit.source: Paul also said that he had not known that the man whom he had insulted was the high priest. (5)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~5#Answer:What did Paul reply?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.7+When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, what did they do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~7#Answer:When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, what did they do?718301833
trans-unit.source: When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, the two groups began to argue violently.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~7#Answer:When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, what did they do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~7#Answer:When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, what did they do?1605007883
trans-unit.source: They argued, because the Pharisees believed what Paul believed, and the Sadducees disagreed with the Pharisees and with Paul. (7)

group.id: Q:ACT 23.8+What did the Sadducees not believe?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~8#Question:What did the Sadducees not believe?
trans-unit.source: What did the Sadducees not believe?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~8#Question:What did the Sadducees not believe?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Sadducees not believe?408484220
trans-unit.source: The Sadducees did not believe that the people who have died will ever become alive again. They also did not believe that there are any angels or other kinds of spirits. (8a-b)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Sadducees not believe?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.8+What did the Pharisees believe?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~8#Question:What did the Pharisees believe?
trans-unit.source: What did the Pharisees believe?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Pharisees believe?-1118624205
trans-unit.source: The Pharisees believed that the time will come when God will cause everyone who has died to become alive again.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Pharisees believe?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Pharisees believe?-1813469039
trans-unit.source: They also believed that there are angels and other kinds of spirits. (8c)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~8#Answer:What did the Pharisees believe?

trans-unit.source: Those Pharisees said that perhaps an angel or some other spirit had spoken to Paul. (9)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~9#Answer:What else did the Pharisees say in order to defend Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.10+What did the commander do when he saw that the Sadducees and Pharisees were fighting violently all around Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.11+In what way did the Lord Jesus encourage Paul at that time?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.16+What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~16#Question:What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?
trans-unit.source: What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~16#Question:What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?

trans-unit.source: Paul's nephew had heard what those Jews had planned.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~16#Answer:What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~16#Answer:What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?-452636381
trans-unit.source: So he went to the barracks where Paul was and told Paul what he had heard. (16)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~16#Answer:What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.17+What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~17#Answer:What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?-1481507201
trans-unit.source: Paul asked one of the officers/centurions to take his nephew to the commander.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~17#Answer:What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~17#Answer:What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?908130186
trans-unit.source: He told the officer/centurion that his nephew needed to tell the commander something. (17)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~17#Answer:What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.20+What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~20#Question:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?
trans-unit.source: What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~20#Question:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?618901406
trans-unit.source: Paul's nephew told the commander that certain Jews were going to ask the commander to order that Paul go to meet again with the Sanhedrin.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?-196277639
trans-unit.source: Those Jews were going to tell the commander that the Sanhedrin needed to ask Paul some more questions.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?-168925900
trans-unit.source: Paul's nephew also told the commander that it was not true that the Sanhedrin wanted to meet with Paul again and ask him more questions. (20)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~20#Answer:What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?

trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Question:What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?

trans-unit.source: What did Paul's nephew ask the commander not to do?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Alternate:What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?

trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Alternate:What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~21#Answer:What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?-830922611
trans-unit.source: Paul's nephew told the commander not to order that Paul go to meet the Sanhedrin again. (21)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Answer:What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.21+What else did he tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~21#Question:What else did he tell the commander?
trans-unit.source: What else did he tell the commander?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Question:What else did he tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?-1979209239
trans-unit.source: He told the commander that more than forty Jews were planning to kill Paul.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?1857269657
trans-unit.source: They had made a promise with each other that they would not eat or drink anything until they had killed him/Paul.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?-1304244105
trans-unit.source: They were already waiting for the commander to order a guard to take Paul to where the Sanhedrin was going to meet.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?-970982570
trans-unit.source: But they/the Jews were going to wait in hiding, and they were going to kill Paul as he was on the way. (21)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~21#Answer:What else did he tell the commander?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.22+After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~22#Question:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?
trans-unit.source: After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~22#Question:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~22#Answer:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?-1816367056
trans-unit.source: The commander told Paul's nephew not to let anyone know what he had told him.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~22#Answer:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~22#Answer:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?1972043028
trans-unit.source: Then the commander dismissed him. (22)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~22#Answer:After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?

trans-unit.id: h:!ACT!23~23#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Acts 23:23-35 The commander sent Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea, escorted by a guard of Roman soldiers.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~23#Section Heading

group.id: Q:ACT 23.23-35+What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~23#Question:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?
trans-unit.source: What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~23#Question:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?-320299802
trans-unit.source: He ordered two of his centurions to assemble a group of 200 foot soldiers, 70 horsemen, and 200 soldiers carrying spears to be ready to leave for Caesarea at nine o'clock that night.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?-553153401
trans-unit.source: They were to provide Paul with two horses to ride.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?813833141
trans-unit.source: Then they were to escort Paul to Caesarea and leave him in the charge of the Governor, Felix. (23-24)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~23#Answer:What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.25-26+What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~25#Question:What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?
trans-unit.source: What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~25#Question:What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~25#Answer:What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?926242441
trans-unit.source: The name of the commander was Claudius Lysias. (25-26)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~25#Answer:What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.27+What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~27#Question:What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?
trans-unit.source: What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~27#Question:What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~27#Answer:What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?859690614
trans-unit.source: He told the Governor that Paul was a Roman citizen, and that he (the commander) had prevented the Jews from killing Paul. (27)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~27#Answer:What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.28+For what reason had Claudius Lysias taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~28#Question:For what reason had Claudius Lysias taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~28#Answer:For what reason had Claudius Lysias taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin?-526337152
trans-unit.source: Claudius Lysias had taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin so that he could find out what Paul had done to cause the Jews to be angry with him. (28)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~28#Answer:For what reason had Claudius Lysias taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.30+What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~30#Question:What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?
trans-unit.source: What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~30#Question:What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~30#Answer:What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?-1586399986
trans-unit.source: He wrote that he had told the Jews, who were accusing Paul, to go to Caesarea and present their charges against Paul before the Governor. (30)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~30#Answer:What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.31-33+Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~31#Question:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.
trans-unit.source: Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~31#Question:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.848741443
trans-unit.source: The soldiers went with Paul as far as [the town] Antipatris that night.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.1265332664
trans-unit.source: The next day, the foot soldiers returned to Jerusalem, while the horsemen went on with Paul to Caesarea.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.-1877133532
trans-unit.source: They gave the Governor the letter from Claudius Lysias and delivered Paul into his care. (31-33)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~31#Answer:Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

group.id: Q:ACT 23.34+What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~34#Question:What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?
trans-unit.source: What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~34#Question:What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~34#Answer:What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?1100330717
trans-unit.source: After the Governor read the letter, he asked Paul what province he was from, and Paul replied, "Cilicia." (34)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~34#Answer:What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.35+What else did the Governor say to Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~35#Question:What else did the Governor say to Paul?
trans-unit.source: What else did the Governor say to Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~35#Question:What else did the Governor say to Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~35#Answer:What else did the Governor say to Paul?-1832587905
trans-unit.source: He told Paul that he would listen to his defense after the Jews, who were accusing him, had come from Jerusalem. (35a)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~35#Answer:What else did the Governor say to Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 23.35+Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!23~35#Question:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?
trans-unit.source: Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~35#Question:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~35#Answer:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?1194587558
trans-unit.source: The Governor gave orders that Paul was to stay in the building that had earlier been Herod's palace.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~35#Answer:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!23~35#Answer:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?1791070083
trans-unit.source: A guard was to be with him all the time. (35b)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!23~35#Answer:Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?

trans-unit.id: h:!ACT!24~1#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Acts 24:1-27 Paul defended himself before the Governor, Felix, and several men of the Sanhedrin.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Section Heading

group.id: Q:ACT 24.1-27+What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~1#Question:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?
trans-unit.source: What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Question:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~1#Answer:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?-605137882
trans-unit.source: Paul told the Governor that only twelve days had passed since he had gone up to Jerusalem. When he was in Jerusalem, the Jews had not found him arguing with anyone in the Temple, nor had they seen him stirring up the people anywhere else in the city of Jerusalem.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Answer:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~1#Answer:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?1090232113
trans-unit.source: Therefore, it was not true that he went everywhere stirring up the Jews to riot. (10-12)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Answer:What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?

group.id: Q:ACT 24.1+Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~1#Question:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?
trans-unit.source: Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Question:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~1#Answer:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?1379500924
trans-unit.source: The high priest, Ananias, and a few other members of the Sanhedrin came from Jerusalem to accuse Paul before Felix.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Answer:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~1#Answer:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?-1550561673
trans-unit.source: A lawyer whose name was Tertullus also came to present his charges against Paul. (1)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~1#Answer:Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?

group.id: Q:ACT 24.5+In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~5#Question:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?
trans-unit.source: In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~5#Question:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?-1338772102
trans-unit.source: Tertullus said that Paul was a dangerous trouble-maker.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?335829742
trans-unit.source: He said that everywhere in the world Paul had stirred up the Jews to riot.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?1794546953
trans-unit.source: He also said that Paul was the leader of a group called the Nazarenes. (5)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~5#Answer:In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?

group.id: Q:ACT 24.6+Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~6#Question:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?
trans-unit.source: Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~6#Question:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~6#Answer:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?468376272
trans-unit.source: Tertullus said that Paul had tried to defile the Temple in Jerusalem.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~6#Answer:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~6#Answer:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?-954994261
trans-unit.source: For those reasons the Jews had had Paul arrested. (6a)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~6#Answer:Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?

group.id: Q:ACT 24.7+Who was Lysius?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~7#Question:Who was Lysius?
trans-unit.source: Who was Lysius?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~7#Question:Who was Lysius?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~7#Answer:Who was Lysius?1344415632
trans-unit.source: The chief captain (of the Roman soldiers in Jerusalem).
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~7#Answer:Who was Lysius?

group.id: Q:ACT 24.7-8+What did Lysius do?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!24~7#Question:What did Lysius do?
trans-unit.source: What did Lysius do?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!24~7#Question:What did Lysius do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!24~7#Answer:What did Lysius do?1772587320
trans-unit.source: He took Paul away from the Jews (rescuing him from what probably would have been "mob justice").

trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~6#Answer:Of what did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul when they stood before Festus in Caesarea?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.8+What did Paul say when he defended himself?

trans-unit.source: What did Paul say when he defended himself?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~8#Answer:What did Paul say when he defended himself?-1557043016
trans-unit.source: He told Festus that he had not done anything against the law of the Jewish religion, nor anything against the Temple.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~8#Answer:What did Paul say when he defended himself?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~8#Answer:What did Paul say when he defended himself?-1223455616
trans-unit.source: He also told Festus that he had not done anything against the Roman Emperor. (8)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~8#Answer:What did Paul say when he defended himself?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.9+What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~9#Question:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?
trans-unit.source: What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~9#Question:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~9#Answer:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?-1697994873
trans-unit.source: They wanted Festus to order Paul to go up to Jerusalem again and to try Paul there.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~9#Answer:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~9#Answer:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?-1576411225
trans-unit.source: So Festus asked Paul if he was willing to return to Jerusalem and have the Jews accuse him there. (9)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~9#Answer:What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.10+What did Paul reply to Festus?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~10#Question:What did Paul reply to Festus?
trans-unit.source: What did Paul reply to Festus?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~10#Question:What did Paul reply to Festus?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~10#Answer:What did Paul reply to Festus?583731056
trans-unit.source: Paul replied that the court of Festus [in Caesarea] was a court of the Roman government, and he had a right to be judged there.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~10#Answer:What did Paul reply to Festus?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~10#Answer:What did Paul reply to Festus?-431207303
trans-unit.source: Paul then repeated that he had done no wrong to the Jews, and that Festus knew that. (10)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~10#Answer:What did Paul reply to Festus?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.11+What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~11#Question:What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?
trans-unit.source: What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Question:What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~11#Answer:What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?-1912982164
trans-unit.source: He also said that if he had committed any crime against the Roman government and deserved to die/be killed, he was willing to die for that crime. (11a)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Answer:What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.11+For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~11#Question:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?
trans-unit.source: For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Question:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?1906986110
trans-unit.source: Paul repeated that he had not done the things of which the Jews accused him.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?694424942
trans-unit.source: The Jews had not been able to prove that Paul had done any wrong to them.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?-1121349517
trans-unit.source: Therefore, no one had the right to give the Jews the authority to judge him. (11b)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Answer:For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.11+What did Paul say to Festus after that?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~11#Question:What did Paul say to Festus after that?
trans-unit.source: What did Paul say to Festus after that?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~11#Answer:What did Paul say to Festus after that?1282205367
trans-unit.source: Paul said, "I appeal to the Emperor (Caesar)!" (11c)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Answer:What did Paul say to Festus after that?

trans-unit.id: n:!ACT!25~11#Note:What did Paul say to Festus after that?-450299855
trans-unit.source: When he said that, Paul was asking that the highest Roman court judge him. The court of the Emperor in Rome was the highest court.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~11#Note:What did Paul say to Festus after that?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.13+Who was King Agrippa?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~13#Question:Who was King Agrippa?
trans-unit.source: Who was King Agrippa?

trans-unit.source: Agrippa was an important official of the Roman government. (13)

trans-unit.id: n:!ACT!25~13#Note:Who was King Agrippa?-342316453
trans-unit.source: King Agrippa ruled over an area northeast of Judea. Bernice was his sister.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~13#Note:Who was King Agrippa?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.13+For what purpose had King Agrippa and Bernice come to Caesarea?

trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~13#Question:For what purpose had King Agrippa and Bernice come to Caesarea?

trans-unit.source: After Festus had become the Governor of Judea, Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to welcome him. (13)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~13#Answer:For what purpose had King Agrippa and Bernice come to Caesarea?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.14+What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~14#Question:What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?
trans-unit.source: What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~14#Question:What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~14#Answer:What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?1709969208
trans-unit.source: Festus told Agrippa that Paul had been left as a prisoner by Felix. (14)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~14#Answer:What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.15+What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~15#Question:What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?
trans-unit.source: What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~15#Question:What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~15#Answer:What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?-2112009977
trans-unit.source: The Jewish leaders had come to him and had made charges against Paul. (15a)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~15#Answer:What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.15+What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~15#Question:What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?
trans-unit.source: What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~15#Answer:What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?-198799898
trans-unit.source: Festus said that the Jewish religious leaders in Jerusalem had asked him to judge/condemn Paul. (15)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~15#Answer:What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.16+What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~16#Question:What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?
trans-unit.source: What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~16#Question:What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~16#Answer:What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?-1596363344
trans-unit.source: Festus said that he had refused to judge/condemn Paul because Paul had not yet had a chance to defend himself against the people who had accused him. (16)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~16#Answer:What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.17+What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~17#Question:What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?
trans-unit.source: What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~17#Question:What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~17#Answer:What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?1371384183
trans-unit.source: Festus said that the day after the Jewish leaders arrived in Caesarea, he had held court, and had sent for Paul in order to judge his case. (17)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~17#Answer:What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.18-19+What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~18#Question:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?
trans-unit.source: What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~18#Question:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~18#Answer:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?-1164998923
trans-unit.source: The Jewish leaders did not accuse Paul of any crime against the Roman government.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~18#Answer:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~18#Answer:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?-1022549152
trans-unit.source: They told Festus only that Paul had argued with them about certain religious beliefs. (18-19a)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~18#Answer:What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.19+What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~19#Question:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?
trans-unit.source: What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~19#Question:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~19#Answer:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?-1374574099
trans-unit.source: Festus told Agrippa that Paul and the Jewish leaders had argued about a man named Jesus.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~19#Answer:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~19#Answer:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?1687133880
trans-unit.source: The Jewish leaders said that Jesus was dead, but Paul claimed that Jesus was alive. (19b)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~19#Answer:What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.20+For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~20#Question:For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?
trans-unit.source: For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~20#Question:For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~20#Answer:For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?1361254987
trans-unit.source: Festus said that he did not feel able to judge Paul's case, because the accusations against Paul were entirely about the Jewish religion. (20)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~20#Answer:For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.21+For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~21#Question:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?
trans-unit.source: For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~21#Question:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~21#Answer:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?788856828
trans-unit.source: Festus told Agrippa that Paul had asked to be judged by the Emperor's court.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~21#Answer:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~21#Answer:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?-1722539401
trans-unit.source: He wanted Agrippa to advise him whether he should do that. (21)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~21#Answer:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?

trans-unit.id: n:!ACT!25~21#Note:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?1727735201
trans-unit.source: In order to be judged by the Emperor's court, Paul would need to go to Rome. So Festus planned to keep Paul under guard until he could send him to Rome.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~21#Note:For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.22+What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~22#Question:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?
trans-unit.source: What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~22#Question:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~22#Answer:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?-1119290881
trans-unit.source: Agrippa said that he himself would like to hear Paul defend himself.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~22#Answer:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~22#Answer:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?-823342044
trans-unit.source: Festus promised him that he would hold court the next day and send for Paul to present himself. (22)
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~22#Answer:What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.24+What did Festus tell King Agrippa and the other people present that the Jews had said about Paul?

trans-unit.source: What did Festus tell King Agrippa and the other people present that the Jews had said about Paul?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~24#Question:What did Festus tell King Agrippa and the other people present that the Jews had said about Paul?

trans-unit.source: What did Festus himself say about Paul?

trans-unit.source: Festus told Agrippa that when he listened to Paul defending himself, he had decided that Paul had not done anything for which he deserved to be executed/killed.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~25#Answer:What did Festus himself say about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~25#Answer:What did Festus himself say about Paul?-825336030
trans-unit.source: However, Paul himself had requested that he be tried/judged by the Emperor in Rome.
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~25#Answer:What did Festus himself say about Paul?

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~25#Answer:What did Festus himself say about Paul?-571987444

trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~25#Answer:What did Festus himself say about Paul?

group.id: Q:ACT 25.26-27+For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?

trans-unit.id: q:!ACT!25~26#Question:For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?
trans-unit.source: For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?
trans-unit.note: !ACT!25~26#Question:For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?

trans-unit.source: He said that there was nothing for which he could charge/accuse Paul, but he was sending him to Rome as a prisoner.

trans-unit.id: a:!ACT!25~26#Answer:For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?-358797286
trans-unit.source: So he wanted Agrippa to tell him what to say about Paul in the letter he was going to send to the Emperor. (26-27)

group.id: Q:ACT 28.26+What did the prophecy of Isaiah mean?

group.id: Q:COL 1.1+Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.note: !COL!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?682361688
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God," with a capital "G," is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god," with a lower case "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word "theos," can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized.
trans-unit.note: !COL!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!COL!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-22475676
trans-unit.source: See "God" in KBT.

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!1~5#Answer:What do you think the gospel is?-317692804
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news, or joyful report, that God has made a way of salvation for sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV, and most modern English versions, as "gospel".
trans-unit.note: !COL!1~5#Answer:What do you think the gospel is?

group.id: Q:COL 3.12-14+How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.source: How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Question:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?-1755402893
trans-unit.source: He told them that they should be compassionate to one-another/have feelings of sympathy toward someone that needs help, show concern for those who need help.
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?1387503825
trans-unit.source: They should be kind to one another/act in helpful, loving ways toward people, behave helpfully toward people, and be "goodhearted".
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?-1292419850
trans-unit.source: They should be humble with one another/not be proud and arrogant, not act as though they/you are better than other people.
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?114481990
trans-unit.source: They should be gentle with one another/willing to give in, not demand their own way, and be considerate of the rights and feelings of other people.
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?-663633544
trans-unit.source: They should be patient with one another/calmly endure unfair or unkind treatment by others, not become angry quickly when other people do something unpleasant. (12)
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?-1813921608
trans-unit.source: They should calmly endure the things which other people do regularly, each day, that annoy them.
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?1567316420
trans-unit.source: They should forgive anyone who has done something wrong against them in the same way that the Lord has forgiven them. (13)
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

trans-unit.id: a:!COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?13493400
trans-unit.source: They should love one another. (14)
trans-unit.note: !COL!3~12#Answer:How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?

group.id: Q:EPH 1.1+Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!EPH!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?-1492694136
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God," with a capital "G," is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god," with a lower case "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and can not be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It can not be pluralised.
trans-unit.note: !EPH!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!EPH!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-22475676
trans-unit.source: See "God" in KBT.

group.id: Q:EPH 1.13+What do you think the gospel is?

trans-unit.note: !EPH!1~13#Question:What do you think the gospel is?

trans-unit.id: a:!EPH!1~13#Answer:What do you think the gospel is?-210372623
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way to save sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV, and in most modern English versions, as "gospel".
trans-unit.note: !EPH!1~13#Answer:What do you think the gospel is?

trans-unit.id: n:!EPH!1~13#Note:What do you think the gospel is?-1635459669
trans-unit.source: See "gospel" in KBT.

trans-unit.source: The Gentile people had previously not known God. As far as the Jews were concerned, the Gentiles were outcasts [from God]. trans-unit.source: Christ ascended to heaven. (8)
trans-unit.note: !EPH!4~8#Answer:Who ascended into a high place?

trans-unit.id: n:!EPH!4~8#Note:Who ascended into a high place?-1169478699
trans-unit.source: According to T.N. on Ephesians, this verse refers to a quote from Psalm 68:18 that describes a Jewish king who had defeated his enemies and was returning in victory. Paul saw that as a picture of Christ ascending to heaven. Just as the king won a victory, and then went up to a high place and gave gifts to people; so also Christ won a victory (over sin and death), and then went up to a high place (God's right side in heaven) and gave gifts (special abilities) to his followers.
trans-unit.note: !EPH!4~8#Note:Who ascended into a high place?

group.id: Q:GAL 1.1+Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: q:!GAL!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?
trans-unit.source: Who do you think God is?
trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?1014921725
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "g" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!GAL!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-1713399034
trans-unit.source: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralised. (Or, if it can be pluralised, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)
trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!1~6#Answer:What do you think the gospel is?-1441958636
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way to save sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV and most modern English versions as "gospel".

trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~8#Question:Do you think an angel from heaven could/would preach a [distorted] message [contrary to the true gospel that Paul was preaching]? // What would it tell you if an angel from heaven preached a message contrary to the truth?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!1~8#Answer:Do you think an angel from heaven could/would preach a [distorted] message [contrary to the true gospel that Paul was preaching]? // What would it tell you if an angel from heaven preached a message contrary to the truth?-1762105080
trans-unit.source: One of God's true angels would never do this. If a being appeared as an angel and spoke false words, this would be a demon/evil spirit.
trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~8#Answer:Do you think an angel from heaven could/would preach a [distorted] message [contrary to the true gospel that Paul was preaching]? // What would it tell you if an angel from heaven preached a message contrary to the truth?

trans-unit.id: n:!GAL!1~8#Note:Do you think an angel from heaven could/would preach a [distorted] message [contrary to the true gospel that Paul was preaching]? // What would it tell you if an angel from heaven preached a message contrary to the truth?-620157021
trans-unit.source: Here Paul's use of this expression is essentially supposing the impossible, since a good angel "from heaven" could never do this (though a person could mistakenly suppose that he had seen an angelic messenger, rather than a demonic one).

group.id: Q:GAL 1.16+Who do you think the Gentiles are?

trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~16#Question:Who do you think the Gentiles are?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!1~16#Answer:Who do you think the Gentiles are?444287373
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: "Gentiles" is usually the English translation of the Greek ta ethnê or related forms. From the viewpoint of the Jews, "Gentiles" referred to all people who were not Jews and who were, therefore, not God's chosen people and did not worship him. When used from the viewpoint of Christians (as frequently in the epistles of Paul), the term often referred to those who did not believe in Jesus Christ. It was also used in some contexts to refer to people of all nations.
trans-unit.note: !GAL!1~16#Answer:Who do you think the Gentiles are?

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: A covenant is a strong, binding agreement made between two people, an act in which they commit themselves to one another. trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?-540378426
trans-unit.source: The first three are sexual sins: sexual immorality, impurity, debauchery/sensuality (indecent conduct);
trans-unit.note: !GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?-1217535431
trans-unit.source: The next two are religious sins: idolatry, witchcraft/sorcery;
trans-unit.note: !GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?1221013904
trans-unit.source: The next eight sins have to do with their relationships with each other: hatred, strife/discord (lack of harmony or agreement between people), jealousy, fits of rage, selfish ambition, dissensions (quarrels which produce divisions between people), divisions (people separate themselves into parties, combinations or cliques), envy;
trans-unit.note: !GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?1069336479
trans-unit.source: The last two specific sins are group sins characterized by a loss of self-control: drunkenness, orgies.
trans-unit.note: !GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?1864110242
trans-unit.source: This is an open list, since the writer recognizes that there are many other similar sins.
trans-unit.note: !GAL!5~19#Answer:What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?

group.id: Q:GAL 5.21+What do you think it means to inherit the kingdom of God?

trans-unit.id: a:!GAL!5~21#Answer:What do you think it means to inherit the kingdom of God?880787332
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In ordinary English the word "inherit" means "to receive something belonging to your father after he dies". But in the use of the term in this passage, where something is inherited from God, there is no thought of anyone dying. The meaning is "to receive something that God has promised to give you, provided that you fulfill certain conditions". To inherit the kingdom of God a Christian/believer enjoys having God rule over him.

trans-unit.source: The serpent persuaded the woman to eat some fruit from the tree - the one which would enable someone to know good and evil. Then the woman also persuaded the man to eat some of the fruit from that tree. Then they were both ashamed. When God came to (visit/see) them, the man blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent. Then God put a curse on the serpent, and also on the woman, and on the man. (The curse applies to all of their descendants.)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!3~1#Answer:Tell me the main events/points/happenings in this account/passage.

trans-unit.source: He said that he would be banished from the land/from his place. He would be banished from God's presence. He would have to wander about without a home. People (who met him) would kill him. (14)

group.id: Q:GEN 4.15+What was God's answer to Cain?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!4~15#Answer:What was God's answer to Cain?-545570412
trans-unit.source: God/He said that, no, people would not kill him. God/He said that, if someone did kill Cain/him, then God would punish the killer seven times more/harder than he had punished Cain. -OR- God said, "No, people will not kill you. If someone does (try to) kill you, I will punish that killer/him seven times harder than I have punished you." (15)

group.id: Q:GEN 8.1-22+Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!8~1#Question:Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.
trans-unit.source: Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!8~1#Question:Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!8~1#Answer:Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.446158187
trans-unit.source: The rain stopped falling, and the water stopped gushing out of the ground. Eventually the large boat came to rest on the earth/ground. The waters continued to go down. After some time Noah released a raven, which flew around until the earth was dry. He also released a dove, but it could not find dry land, so it returned. He sent it out again a week later, and it returned with a leaf. When he released it again, a week later, it did not return. Eventually the earth dried up, and God told Noah that he and his family and all the creatures on the large boat were to leave the boat/and God told Noah to take his family and all the creatures off/out of the large boat.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!8~1#Answer:Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.

trans-unit.id: h:!GEN!12~10#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Genesis 12:10-20 Abram and Sarai (and their servants) traveled to/went to Egypt.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!12~10#Section Heading

group.id: Q:GEN 12.10-20+Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!12~10#Question:Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?
trans-unit.source: Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!12~10#Question:Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!12~10#Answer:Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?621587174
trans-unit.source: Because of a famine, Abram and Sarai went to Egypt. Abram was afraid that people of Egypt would kill him in order to take his wife. So Abram told Sarai to say/had Sarai say that she was his sister. Pharaoh took Sarai into his harem/to be his wife; but then God sent a terrible plague upon Pharaoh's household. Pharaoh (discovered the source of the plague and) became very angry with Abram, because Abram had not been fully honest/had not told the whole truth. Therefore, Pharaoh deported/expelled Abram and his household from Egypt.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!12~10#Answer:Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?

group.id: Q:GEN 12.10+What was the reason why Abram went to Egypt?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!12~10#Answer:What was the reason why Abram went to Egypt?-243896167
trans-unit.source: Abram went to Egypt [so he and his household would have food,] because there was a famine in Canaan. (10)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!12~10#Answer:What was the reason why Abram went to Egypt?

group.id: Q:GEN 12.11-12+What was Abram worried about?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!12~11#Answer:What was Abram worried about?-907962741

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!12~19#Answer:What did Pharaoh do next?-150102048
trans-unit.source: Pharaoh then deported Abram and all those with him from Egypt. -OR- Pharaoh told Abram to leave Egypt with all his family and servants. (19-20)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!12~19#Answer:What did Pharaoh do next?

group.id: Q:GEN 12.18-19+In your opinion, did Abram behave in an honorable way?

group.id: Q:GEN 14.17-24+Tell what happened when Abram returned from the battle.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!14~17#Answer:Tell what happened when Abram returned from the battle.-1498691352
trans-unit.source: The king of Sodom, and Melchizedek (who was king of Salem, and was also a priest) came to him (Abram). Melchizedek blessed Abram, and Abram gave to Melchizedek a tenth of what he (Abram) had recovered from/in the battle. The king of Sodom then told Abram that he (Abram) could keep the rest of the property that Abram had recovered, but Abram did not accept it.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!14~17#Answer:Tell what happened when Abram returned from the battle.

group.id: Q:GEN 14.18+What do you think was the work of a priest?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!14~18#Question:What do you think was the work of a priest?
trans-unit.source: What do you think was the work of a priest?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!14~18#Question:What do you think was the work of a priest?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!14~18#Answer:What do you think was the work of a priest?-886969539
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: During the time of the Old Testament, people understood that they could not simply approach God on their own. A priest was a "go-between" or mediator between people and God. A priest would offer sacrifices to God on behalf of God's people. A priest would also burn incense, offer prayers, and lead the people in worshipping God.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!14~18#Answer:What do you think was the work of a priest?

trans-unit.id: n:!GEN!14~18#Note:What do you think was the work of a priest?1321972067
trans-unit.source: See "priest" in KBT.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!14~18#Note:What do you think was the work of a priest?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!14~19#Answer:We learn that Melchizedek brought Abram food and drink/bread and wine. What else did Melchizedek do for Abram?-1277408221
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: On several previous occasions, God has blessed people or animals (Genesis 1:22, 28; 5:2; 9:1; 12:2-3). In this passage/section the author wrote that Melchizedek blessed Abram. group.id: Q:GEN 16.1-16+Tell what happened at the time of this account.

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!16~1#Question:Tell what happened at the time of this account.
trans-unit.source: Tell what happened at the time of this account.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!16~1#Question:Tell what happened at the time of this account.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!16~1#Answer:Tell what happened at the time of this account.886116959
trans-unit.source: Sarai, Abram's wife, had so far been unable to bear Abram a child. So she gave to Abram her servant, an Egyptian woman named Hagar, to bear a child for Abram. Hagar became pregnant, and then became disrespectful to Sarai. So Sarai made life miserable for Hagar, and Hagar then fled/ran away. An angel met Hagar, and told her to return to Abram. The angel also told Hagar that she would have a son, that she should name the boy "Ishmael", and that Ishmael would quarrel continually/not be at peace/not get along with his brothers.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!16~1#Answer:Tell what happened at the time of this account.

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: Sarai said in this account/passage that God should examine her and Abram, and that God should decide/pass judgment concerning who was at fault. trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: To circumcise a man or boy is to surgically cut off a specific piece of skin from the end of his penis. trans-unit.source: One day, three men (angels? or two angels and God himself?) suddenly appeared where Abraham's tent was set up. He rushed around to prepare them a meal. Then one of them predicted that Sarah would certainly have a son in about a year. Sarah overheard the conversation and she laughed silently, because she and Abraham were very old/were so old. God asked why Sarah had laughed. God pointed out that nothing is too difficult for him.

group.id: Q:GEN 18.16-33+Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!18~16#Question:Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?
trans-unit.source: Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~16#Question:Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!18~16#Answer:Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?-958985680
trans-unit.source: Abraham was speaking with God. God said that he was going to destroy Sodom because the people were so/very wicked. But Abraham asked God not to destroy the city if there were 50 good people. God agreed to Abraham's request. Then Abraham lowered the number to 45, then 40, then 30, 20, and finally 10. And in each case, God agreed to spare the city for the sake of a few good people. Then God went on his way, and Abraham returned to his tent.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~16#Answer:Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?

trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Alternate:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?

trans-unit.id: l:!GEN!18~20#Alternate:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?2035518464
trans-unit.source: What do you think the "cries" were like that God says he had heard?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Alternate:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!18~20#Answer:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?880588171
trans-unit.source: God knows everything. He might have received a "report" from angels, but he was not getting information that was news to him.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Answer:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!18~20#Answer:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?-751173314
trans-unit.source: Most likely, the "cries" are figurative. (Matthew Poole's Commentary: "Sins are said to cry when they are gross, and manifest, and impudent, and such as highly provoke God to anger.")
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Answer:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?

trans-unit.id: n:!GEN!18~20#Note:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?-1155157197
trans-unit.source: Depending on the respondent's preconceptions regarding the nature of God, this might not be obvious. Ensure that the translation is at least ambiguous and does not suggest outright that God had just learned about the situation via a report or accusation.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Note:How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?

group.id: Q:GEN 18.20-21+What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?

trans-unit.source: What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Question:What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!18~20#Answer:What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?658803353
trans-unit.source: He went there to find out/see for himself (or to show that he had personally witnessed the evidence) if the reports of evil were true. (20-21)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Answer:What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?

trans-unit.id: n:!GEN!18~20#Note:What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?-31764328
trans-unit.source: Benson Commentary: "Not as if there were any thing concerning which God is in doubt; but he is pleased thus to express himself after the manner of men, and to show that he ascertains the criminal’s guilt before he passes sentence."
trans-unit.note: !GEN!18~20#Note:What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?

group.id: Q:GEN 19.1-29+Tell what happened at this time.

trans-unit.note: !GEN!19~1#Question:Tell what happened at this time.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!19~1#Answer:Tell what happened at this time.717988279
trans-unit.source: The two angels went to Sodom, and Lot persuaded them to stay overnight at his house. The men of Sodom tried to take the two visitors and rape them. In order to protect themselves and Lot's family, the angels struck the rioting men blind/with blindness/caused the rioting men to become blind. The next morning, the two visitors/visiting angels grabbed Lot and his wife and two daughters and led them out of the city. Sodom and Gomorrah - and the whole plain - were destroyed.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!19~1#Answer:Tell what happened at this time.

group.id: Q:GEN 19.30-38+Tell what happened after Lot and his daughters had fled the wicked city of Sodom.

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!19~30#Question:Tell what happened after Lot and his daughters had fled the wicked city of Sodom.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!19~30#Answer:Tell what happened after Lot and his daughters had fled the wicked city of Sodom.-1627987813
trans-unit.source: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and lived in a cave in the mountains. The daughters were upset because they had no husbands. Thus they could not have children to carry on the family line. They influenced/induced their father to become drunk, and each of them then had sexual relations with Lot. From each of those two children born, a nation of many people eventually came into being/eventually emerged.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!19~30#Answer:Tell what happened after Lot and his daughters had fled the wicked city of Sodom.

trans-unit.source: They went to a place called Gerar, and while they were there, they said that Sarah was Abraham's sister. King Abimelech took Sarah into his palace (to be one of his concubines). But God came to the king in a dream and told him that Sarah was Abraham's wife. God also caused Abimelech's wife and the other women of the royal household to be barren/unable to become pregnant. So the king returned Sarah to Abraham, along with a gift of sheep and oxen and servants, and much silver (money). Abraham prayed to God, and God then healed Abimelech and his household.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!20~1#Answer:Tell what Abraham and Sarah did here/at this time, and what was the outcome.

trans-unit.source: Sarah was upset at the idea of Ishmael having a part of Isaac's inheritance. She insisted that Abraham send away Ishmael and his mother, Hagar. So Abraham sent them out into the wilderness. Ishmael nearly died of thirst, but suddenly Hagar heard a voice promising that Ishmael would live and that his descendants would become a great nation. Then God showed Hagar some water, and Ishmael's life was spared. He grew up in the wilderness, became an archer, and eventually married/took a woman from Egypt for his wife.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!21~8#Answer:Tell what happened at this time/at the time of this account.

trans-unit.source: No - God was "with" Ishmael. -OR- God was caring for/watching over Ishmael. (20)

trans-unit.id: n:!GEN!21~20#Note:Did God forget about Ishmael while he was growing up?1191121365
trans-unit.source: The expression, "God with" occurs at least sixteen times in Genesis (21:20, 22; 26:3, 24, 28; 28:15, 20; 31:3, 5, 42; 35:3; 39:2, 3, 21, 23; 48:21). In these various contexts, God being "with" someone means that He was providing for them, or guiding them, or protecting them - He was caring for them.

trans-unit.source: King Abimelech came to Abraham and asked him to promise that he would deal fairly/truthfully with Abimelech. trans-unit.id: h:!GEN!22~1#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Genesis 22:1-24 God tested Abraham's faith by commanding/requesting him to sacrifice Isaac.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Section Heading

group.id: Q:GEN 22.1-24+What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!22~1#Question:What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?
trans-unit.source: What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Question:What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!22~1#Answer:What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?165402700
trans-unit.source: God told Abraham to take Isaac, his beloved son, to a mountain, where Abraham was to kill Isaac and to offer/sacrifice him as a burnt offering to God. Abraham obeyed God, and at the last minute, God told Abraham not to harm Isaac. Then God provided a ram for a sacrifice, instead of Isaac. God repeated his blessing-promise to Abraham. Finally, Abraham heard about the many sons that his brother, Nahor, had.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Answer:What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?

group.id: Q:GEN 22.1+For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!22~1#Question:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?
trans-unit.source: For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Question:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!22~1#Answer:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?-64392367
trans-unit.source: God did this to test Abraham's faith - to demonstrate that Abraham believed that whatever God said is true/right. (1)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Answer:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!22~1#Answer:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?2064836062
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: This is a key passage for understanding the Biblical teaching about "faith" or "believing". It had been many years since God first promised that Abraham's descendants would be as numerous as the stars of the sky. God had said that his promise was to be fulfilled through Isaac. At this time, God has told Abraham to sacrifice Isaac. God was asking Abraham to believe that he (God) would fulfill his promise, even though it looked absolutely/completely impossible.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Answer:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?

trans-unit.id: n:!GEN!22~1#Note:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?1410935846
trans-unit.source: See "believe" in KBT.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!22~1#Note:For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?

trans-unit.id: h:!GEN!24~1#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Genesis 24:1-67 Isaac married Rebekah.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!24~1#Section Heading

group.id: Q:GEN 24.1-67+Tell what happened in this chapter.

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!24~1#Question:Tell what happened in this chapter.
trans-unit.source: Tell what happened in this chapter.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!24~1#Question:Tell what happened in this chapter.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!24~1#Answer:Tell what happened in this chapter.-1698674295
trans-unit.source: Abraham had become very old, and his son, Isaac, still had no wife. So Abraham sent a trusted servant back to Abraham's homeland to get/find a wife for Isaac. Abraham's servant asked/requested God to lead him to the woman of God's choice. The servant asked/requested of God that if a certain woman was God's choice, that when the servant asked her for some drinking water, then she would give him some. He also asked/requested God that the woman of God's choice would offer to get/draw/bring him water for his (the servant's) camels. As soon as the servant finished praying/making that request of God, a young woman named Rebekah appeared. She was the daughter of Isaac's cousin, Bethuel. When Abraham's servant asked her for a drink, she gave him one and offered to get/draw/bring water for his camels, also. The servant watched her, and then gave her some jewelry, and asked/questioned her about her family. When the servant learned that Rebekah was from Abraham's family, he praised God. He went with Rebekah to her home, and explained everything to her family. Her family agreed that Rebekah could go with that servant to marry Isaac - but they wanted her to stay a little while longer. The servant wanted to return home to Canaan soon, and Rebekah agreed that she would go with him. As they were arriving back in Canaan, Rebekah saw a man in the field - it turned out to be Isaac. They were married, and Rebekah comforted Isaac over/in the death/loss of his mother.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!24~1#Answer:Tell what happened in this chapter.

group.id: Q:GEN 25.27-34+Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!25~27#Question:Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.
trans-unit.source: Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!25~27#Question:Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!25~27#Answer:Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.1744496115
trans-unit.source: Esau became a skillful hunter, while Jacob preferred to stay home. One day Esau came in from hunting. He was tired and hungry. Jacob was cooking some stew, so Esau asked for some of it. Jacob told Esau that he could have some, but only if Esau swore/promised to give up his rights as the firstborn son to Jacob. So Esau agreed to do that, and he did not seem to regret his action.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!25~27#Answer:Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.

group.id: Q:GEN 25.27-34+What do you think about the way the two young men behaved in this incident?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!25~27#Question:What do you think about the way the two young men behaved in this incident?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!25~27#Answer:What do you think about the way the two young men behaved in this incident?727276038
trans-unit.source: Probably it was not appropriate for Jacob to manipulate his brother in this way. And it was quite certainly not appropriate for Esau to care so little about his birthright.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!25~27#Answer:What do you think about the way the two young men behaved in this incident?

trans-unit.note: !GEN!26~6#Question:Tell what took place at this time.

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!26~6#Answer:Tell what took place at this time.-193233694
trans-unit.source: Isaac and Rebekah were staying at/in Gerar. When the men of Gerar asked about Rebekah, Isaac said that she was his sister, because he was afraid that if people knew that she was his wife, then they might kill him to take her. But one day Abimelech, the king, saw Isaac embracing Rebekah, and scolded Isaac for not telling others that she was his wife. So Abimelech told everyone not to harm Isaac or Rebekah.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!26~6#Answer:Tell what took place at this time.
