trans-unit.source: No, she was not buried there, because she had died while Jacob and his family were traveling. (35:16-20)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!49~31#Answer:Was Jacob's favorite wife, Rachel, buried at the same place?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~4#Answer:What did Joseph do after that?332923231
trans-unit.source: He sent someone to request Pharaoh to allow him (Joseph) to take his father's corpse to Canaan in order to bury him there. (4-5)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~4#Answer:What did Joseph do after that?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.4-5+What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~4#Question:What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?
trans-unit.source: What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~4#Question:What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~4#Answer:What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?55318611
trans-unit.source: Perhaps he did that, because he was mourning (for) his father in Goshen. Perhaps it was not acceptable for Joseph to come near [to] Pharaoh at that time, because Joseph had been near/had touched a corpse. (4-5)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~4#Answer:What do you think was the reason why Joseph sent a message to Pharaoh, rather than going himself?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.4-5+What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~4#Question:What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?
trans-unit.source: What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~4#Question:What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~4#Answer:What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?-723688193
trans-unit.source: Joseph told Pharaoh about the promise that he (Joseph) had made to his father. He (Joseph) had promised to bury Jacob in Canaan. (Therefore) Joseph asked Pharaoh to allow him to go to bury Jacob's corpse in Canaan. (4-5)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~4#Answer:What was Joseph's message to Pharaoh?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.5+What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~5#Question:What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?

trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~5#Question:What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?

trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~5#Alternate:What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~5#Answer:What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?240618713
trans-unit.source: Joseph promised that he would return to Egypt, when he (Joseph) had completed burying his father's corpse. (5)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~5#Answer:What did Joseph promise/say to assure Pharaoh at that time?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.6+What was Pharaoh's response?

trans-unit.source: What was Pharaoh's response?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~6#Question:What was Pharaoh's response?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~6#Answer:What was Pharaoh's response?843615075
trans-unit.source: Pharaoh (sent a servant back to Joseph, who) said that Joseph could/was free to fulfill his promise to his father. He could/was free to go to Canaan to bury Jacob. (6)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~6#Answer:What was Pharaoh's response?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.7-8+Who went along to Canaan with Joseph?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~7#Question:Who went along to Canaan with Joseph?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~7#Answer:Who went along to Canaan with Joseph?-2063361934
trans-unit.source: Many people accompanied Joseph: Egyptian officials, elders of Pharaoh's household/Pharaoh's senior officers, and Pharaoh's advisors. Also, Joseph's brothers and Jacob's extended family went along, except for the small children. (7-8)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~7#Answer:Who went along to Canaan with Joseph?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.9+Did they have anyone to protect them on their long journey?

trans-unit.source: Yes, there were soldiers riding on horses and in chariots/carts. (9)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~9#Answer:Did they have anyone to protect them on their long journey?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~10#Answer:While they were traveling, where did they stop and mourn for Jacob?2036427108

trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~10#Answer:While they were traveling, where did they stop and mourn for Jacob?

trans-unit.source: How long did they mourn there?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~10#Answer:How long did they mourn there?323170574
trans-unit.source: They mourned there for seven days. (10)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~10#Answer:How long did they mourn there?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.12-13+By what means did Jacob's sons show respect for their father?

trans-unit.source: By what means did Jacob's sons show respect for their father?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~12#Answer:By what means did Jacob's sons show respect for their father?-1089688350
trans-unit.source: They obeyed his (final) request and buried him in the Cave of Machpelah, in Canaan. (12-13)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~12#Answer:By what means did Jacob's sons show respect for their father?

trans-unit.source: Then what did Joseph do?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~14#Question:Then what did Joseph do?

trans-unit.source: He returned to Egypt (as he had promised [to] Pharaoh). (14)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~14#Answer:Then what did Joseph do?

trans-unit.source: Genesis 50:15-21 Joseph and his brothers.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~15#Section Heading

group.id: Q:GEN 50.15-21+After Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt, of what were they afraid?

trans-unit.source: After Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt, of what were they afraid?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~15#Question:After Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt, of what were they afraid?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~15#Answer:After Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt, of what were they afraid?1666682363
trans-unit.source: They were afraid that, since their father was now dead, perhaps Joseph was still angry with them. They were afraid that he might take revenge for the way that they had sold him as a slave to Egypt.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~15#Answer:After Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt, of what were they afraid?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.15-21+Was Joseph planning to take revenge?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~15#Question:Was Joseph planning to take revenge?
trans-unit.source: Was Joseph planning to take revenge?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~15#Question:Was Joseph planning to take revenge?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~15#Answer:Was Joseph planning to take revenge?266723254
trans-unit.source: No. Joseph knew that God had been caring for him all those years, and that what happened to him was part of God's plan.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~15#Answer:Was Joseph planning to take revenge?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.16-17+Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~16#Question:Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?
trans-unit.source: Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~16#Question:Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~16#Answer:Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?2147133683
trans-unit.source: They sent a message to Joseph. In their message, they said that their father wanted Joseph to forgive his brothers. (16-17)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~16#Answer:Because Joseph's brothers were afraid of Joseph, what did they do?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.17+What did Joseph do when he received their message?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~17#Question:What did Joseph do when he received their message?
trans-unit.source: What did Joseph do when he received their message?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~17#Question:What did Joseph do when he received their message?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~17#Answer:What did Joseph do when he received their message?800741095
trans-unit.source: He cried. (17)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~17#Answer:What did Joseph do when he received their message?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.17+In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~17#Question:In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?
trans-unit.source: In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~17#Question:In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~17#Answer:In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?1839911415
trans-unit.source: Perhaps Joseph was sad that his father and brothers supposed that he (Joseph) might take revenge. Or perhaps Joseph was sad as he thought again of his father, or of the pain that he would have experienced when his own brothers plotted to kill him and then sold him as a slave.
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~17#Answer:In your opinion, what caused Joseph to cry when he received the message from his brothers?

group.id: Q:GEN 50.18+What else did the brothers do at that time?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~18#Question:What else did the brothers do at that time?
trans-unit.source: What else did the brothers do at that time?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~18#Question:What else did the brothers do at that time?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~18#Answer:What else did the brothers do at that time?1701224769
trans-unit.source: They went and bowed low in front of Joseph, and offered to be his slaves. (18)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~18#Answer:What else did the brothers do at that time?

trans-unit.id: q:!GEN!50~19#Question:What was Joseph's answer to them?
trans-unit.source: What was Joseph's answer to them?
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~19#Question:What was Joseph's answer to them?

trans-unit.id: a:!GEN!50~19#Answer:What was Joseph's answer to them?1334410167
trans-unit.source: Joseph told them not to be afraid. He said that he was not God, and thus he did not have the authority to judge and punish/and take revenge on his brothers. (19)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~19#Answer:What was Joseph's answer to them?

trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~19#Question:Who does have the authority to judge and punish someone who has done wrong?

trans-unit.source: God has that authority. (19)
trans-unit.note: !GEN!50~19#Answer:Who does have the authority to judge and punish someone who has done wrong?

group.id: Q:HEB 1.4-14+Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!1~4#Question:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?
trans-unit.source: Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!1~4#Question:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!1~4#Answer:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?-238156309
trans-unit.source: These Hebrew Christians were thinking about leaving Christianity and their believing in Jesus Christ as God's Son and going back into their old religion, Judaism. In that religion, the Jews had come to think that God was very far away, and in order to communicate with God, the gap had to be filled with beings like angels. Angels were thought of as very important and were worshipped. But the Son is the only one between God and man, and people are to worship only him.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!1~4#Answer:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?

trans-unit.id: n:!HEB!1~4#Note:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?-1548283520
trans-unit.source: A sharp respondent will probably say the purpose was to teach them that they were not to worship angels. That is about all you can expect them to know of this unless the information is in the introduction.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!1~4#Note:Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?

group.id: Q:HEB 5.8-10+It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!5~8#Question:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?
trans-unit.source: It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!5~8#Question:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!5~8#Answer:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?1463063849
trans-unit.source: It was hard for him to die on the Cross and endure having God turn his back on him. Furthermore he was a man as well as God's Son. And as man's representative before God, he must go through what people go through to learn obedience. There may be other reasons, but always in contrast to our usual reason of sinfulness.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!5~8#Answer:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?

trans-unit.id: n:!HEB!5~8#Note:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?1929729158
trans-unit.source: These answers are primarily for the translator, as very few respondents will be able to give these reasons. The translator should just be sure that the respondent does not understand a wrong reason.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!5~8#Note:It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?

trans-unit.source: It is the same with the people as it is with the ground. Their hearts are like the ground and God's Message is like the rain. When God has spoken to them they should become and live like people who are spiritually mature/adults in God's ways. When they do, God blesses them. But if they remain useless to him, they are in danger of being cursed by him and destroyed the same way useless weeds are burned.

group.id: Q:HEB 9.23-28+Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!9~23#Answer:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.-1085819915
trans-unit.source: The tent/place of worship here on earth was only a copy of the place in heaven. The sacrifice to prepare that place had to be far greater than the sacrifice required to prepare the place here on earth. Jesus's sacrifice was that greater sacrifice. trans-unit.source: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~3#Answer:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.2059572117
trans-unit.source: They are to consider how Jesus endured much suffering to the end and did not give up. They are to be encouraged, after all they have not yet been persecuted to the point of being killed.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Answer:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.source: What does the writer tell them to do?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Question:What does the writer tell them to do?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~3#Answer:What does the writer tell them to do?-702053521

trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Answer:What does the writer tell them to do?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.3+What about him are they to consider?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~3#Question:What about him are they to consider?
trans-unit.source: What about him are they to consider?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Question:What about him are they to consider?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~3#Answer:What about him are they to consider?288365270
trans-unit.source: He did not give up trusting God even when men did such terrible things to him and said such terrible things about him.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Answer:What about him are they to consider?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.3+Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~3#Question:Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?
trans-unit.source: Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Question:Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~3#Answer:Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?-873098024
trans-unit.source: He wanted them to be encouraged and not give up when they are also persecuted.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~3#Answer:Why did he want them to consider these things about Christ?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.4+Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~4#Question:Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?
trans-unit.source: Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~4#Question:Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~4#Answer:Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?750081202
trans-unit.source: Christ's situation was harder than theirs. He had to die because he trusted God and they had not yet been persecuted to that extent.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~4#Answer:Why should considering Christ's situation encourage them?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.4+How hard was his situation?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~4#Question:How hard was his situation?
trans-unit.source: How hard was his situation?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~4#Question:How hard was his situation?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~4#Answer:How hard was his situation?856333800
trans-unit.source: He suffered much more than any other human has ever done in his struggle with temptation as he faced death and separation from his Father, and yet he did not give up.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~4#Answer:How hard was his situation?

trans-unit.id: n:!HEB!12~4#Note:How hard was his situation?-13654919
trans-unit.source: A respondent will probably only say he died rather than give up.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~4#Note:How hard was his situation?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.26-27+What else does he say here about God speaking here on earth and his speaking from heaven?

trans-unit.source: It says when he spoke from the mountain the earth shook, but when he speaks the next time/again, he will speak from heaven and not only the earth, but the heavens will shake once and for all.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~26#Answer:What else does he say here about God speaking here on earth and his speaking from heaven?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.26-27+What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~26#Question:What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?
trans-unit.source: What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~26#Question:What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~26#Answer:What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?565166291
trans-unit.source: It means everything he has created will be shaken and only the things he made to last forever will remain. In other words, the material creation will be removed and he will make everything new and different so that it will last forever.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~26#Answer:What does he mean when he says he will shake the earth and the heavens once and for all?

group.id: Q:HEB 12.25+It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!12~25#Question:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?
trans-unit.source: It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~25#Question:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!12~25#Answer:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?823501317
trans-unit.source: It apparently means that when he "spoke the first time," gave the Old Agreement, he gave it through Moses, a man of the earth, and when he gave the New Agreement he gave it through Jesus, the Man from heaven. (See 2:2, 3.)
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~25#Answer:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?

trans-unit.id: n:!HEB!12~25#Note:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?257936018
trans-unit.source: It is unlikely that any respondent would understand that unless at least part of the implicit information is made explicit.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~25#Note:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?

trans-unit.id: n:!HEB!12~25#Note:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?-265806332
trans-unit.source: The translator should be sure that the respondent understands that all the references in these verses to the mountain, Mt. Sinai, etc., are referring to when God spoke to the ancestors of the Jews long ago and gave them the Old Agreement.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!12~25#Note:It says he spoke to the ancestors from the mountain and now he is speaking to us from heaven. What does that mean?

group.id: Q:HEB 13.10-14+Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.id: q:!HEB!13~10#Question:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
trans-unit.source: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~10#Question:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.id: a:!HEB!13~10#Answer:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.612888367
trans-unit.source: The payment for people's sins was Jesus's death on the Cross. It was a shameful way to die, outside the city. But he was willing to bear that shame to pay for their sins. Now if they who serve him go back to the old ways of keeping Jewish laws because they are ashamed of him, there is no help for them. So let them follow him and bear the shame as he did. After all this world is not their home. Their real home is in heaven.
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~10#Answer:Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

trans-unit.source: He died outside the city.

trans-unit.source: Why?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~11#Question:Why?

trans-unit.source: Why?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~11#Alternate:Why?

trans-unit.source: Why did Jesus die outside the city?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~11#Alternate:Why?

trans-unit.source: Why did Jesus need to die outside the city?
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~11#Alternate:Why?

trans-unit.source: Because when the Jewish high priest took the blood of an animal that had been sacrificed and went into God's presence to offer payment for the people's sins, that animal could not be eaten, it had to be burned outside the city. (So Jesus died outside the city so his blood would be acceptable as payment for people's sins.)
trans-unit.note: !HEB!13~11#Answer:Why?

trans-unit.id: a:!JAS!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?792595772
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "g" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralised.
trans-unit.note: !JAS!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!JAS!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-22475676
trans-unit.source: See "God" in KBT.

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: "Tribe" may refer to an extended family within a nation who are descended from a common ancestor, as in the case of the twelve tribes of Israel, who are descended from the twelve sons of Israel. (See "tribe" in KBT in the "gentile" entry and the "Levite" entry.)

trans-unit.source: James 3:13-18 James told the Christians that there are two kinds of wisdom, earthly wisdom and heavenly wisdom. All Christians should choose the wisdom that God gives.

trans-unit.id: a:!JAS!5~14#Answer:What do you think it means to anoint someone?632005972
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In this context it was done as a symbolic act when praying to God to heal a sick person. The disciples of Jesus often anointed sick people with oil when they asked God to heal them. Probably they poured or smeared oil on the forehead of the person. In this context the action seems to have been symbolic, although rubbing or massaging a person with oil was also practiced as a medical treatment in the ancient world.

group.id: Q:JHN 1.1-5+Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: q:!JHN!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?
trans-unit.source: Who do you think God is?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?-1302093219
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-1713399034
trans-unit.source: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralised. (Or, if it can be pluralised, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?

group.id: Q:JHN 1.24-25+What do you know about Pharisees?

trans-unit.source: What do you know about Pharisees?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~24#Question:What do you know about Pharisees?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!1~24#Answer:What do you know about Pharisees?521969525
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The Semitic words mean "the separated ones," which was transliterated into Greek. It came to mean a certain group of Jewish people. So the idea of "separated" does not need to be included here. The name "Pharisee" means "the separated ones." They were the largest and most important of the Jewish religious groups. They controlled the synagogues and exercised great control over the general population. They taught that the way to God was through obeying the law. They opposed Jesus because He refused to accept the teachings of their oral law.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~24#Answer:What do you know about Pharisees?

group.id: Q:JHN 1.29+What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!1~29#Answer:What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?2044039211
trans-unit.source: God had told the Jews to sacrifice a lamb, which would die for their sins. John meant that now. God was giving his only son, Jesus, to die for all people, so that God would forgive their sins.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~29#Answer:What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!1~29#Note:What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?9725783
trans-unit.source: Check for wrong implications here. In Moslem cultures, or other cultures where lambs are sacrificed, they may be able to pick up the implication that Jesus is the one who will be the sacrifice through which God will forgive sins. In such cultures, check that the appropriate word has been used for "lamb" to suggest this idea. (See "lamb of God" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.)
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~29#Note:What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!1~29#Answer:What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?1823839563
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender, as he deserved. If the one who offended repents and accepts this forgiveness, the result is that the relationship between the two, which was broken by the offense, is restored and the guilt of the offender is removed.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!1~29#Answer:What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!2~13#Answer:What do you know about the Feast of Passover?1483991063
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: This feast was to remember how God's angel passed over the homes of the Jews when they were slaves in Egypt. The angel passed over them because they had put the blood of a perfect lamb on their door posts as a sign. The Egyptians did not do as God had said/ordered/commanded/decreed, so the angel killed the oldest son and the firstborn animal (young) in every such house. Because of that, the Egyptians allowed the Jews to leave Egypt to return to the land God had given to the Jews' ancestor, Abraham, and to his descendants. (See "Passover" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.)
trans-unit.note: !JHN!2~13#Answer:What do you know about the Feast of Passover?

group.id: Q:JHN 3.5+What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!3~5#Answer:What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?1433704008
trans-unit.source: The act of being "born of water" is when someone is put under the water by someone else. This symbolizes the person's decision to repent of his past sins and to do those things that the Lord requires of him from now on. His old way of living is now "washed" away by the water.

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!3~5#Answer:What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?866551347

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!3~5#Answer:What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?1579918199
trans-unit.source: "Water" is used as a symbol of God's cleansing power (as described in Ezekiel 26:25-27).
trans-unit.note: !JHN!3~5#Answer:What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: A Jew was a member of the nation of Palestine from the 6th century B.C. to the first century A.D. It refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. group.id: Q:JHN 4.9+What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!4~9#Answer:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?-1927833518
trans-unit.source: She was surprised because Jesus was a Jew, and the woman was a Samaritan. (9)
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~9#Answer:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!4~9#Note:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?1824111005
trans-unit.source: The Jews never used the same dishes that Samaritans used. An alternative interpretation (less likely) is this: The Jews did not usually have anything to do with the Samaritans.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~9#Note:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!4~9#Note:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?-147878980
trans-unit.source: According to the T.H., there was a Jewish religious regulation in force around A.D. 65 which stated that Samaritan women were in a state of perpetual ritual impurity from the time of their birth; and anyone, who had contact with them, would share that ritual impurity. For that reason the Jews did not use dishes in common with the Samaritans.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~9#Note:What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?

group.id: Q:JHN 4.10+To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?

trans-unit.source: To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~10#Question:To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!4~10#Note:To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?544937631
trans-unit.source: "I do not know" would be an acceptable answer here. The main point of this question would be to check that there are no wrong implications. The most likely explanation is that he was referring to the Holy Spirit, often symbolized by water in John's gospel. Another possibility is that he was referring to the Jewish Law, from which Jesus quoted, and which in Rabbinical literature, was sometimes referred to as "God's gift".
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~10#Note:To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?

group.id: Q:JHN 4.23+What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?

trans-unit.id: q:!JHN!4~23#Question:What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?
trans-unit.source: What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~23#Question:What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!4~23#Note:What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?2110619837
trans-unit.source: "I do not know" would be an acceptable answer. There are various interpretations of this verse. According to Exegetical Helps, "spirit" could mean man's spirit or the Spirit of God. The T.H. states, that wherever the word "spirit" occurs unmarked in John's Gospel, the reference is to God's spirit. According to the NIV Commentary it is not likely that "spirit" here means the Holy Spirit. The human spirit is in mind here. One must worship, not simply outwardly but, in ones spirit. For "truth" the T.H. states that, in this Gospel, "truth" refers primarily to God himself.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~23#Note:What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?

group.id: Q:JHN 4.35+What were people saying?

trans-unit.source: What were people saying?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~35#Question:What were people saying?

trans-unit.id: a:!JHN!4~35#Answer:What were people saying?1394925
trans-unit.source: They said that it was still four months until the time to harvest their grain. (35)
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~35#Answer:What were people saying?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!4~35#Note:What were people saying?-2114899583
trans-unit.source: There are two possible interpretations here. (a) that this was a proverb, and the meaning is that the time from planting to harvest is four months (i.e. there is always a set time of waiting and maturing.) In this case the "do you not say" would refer to a proverbial saying that was generally said, and "you" refers to people in general; Or (b) that from the time when Jesus was speaking, it was still four months until the harvest would be ready. In this case, the "you" would refer to the disciples. Commentators tell us that it was actually six months from planting time to harvest, so interpretation (b) is probably more likely.
trans-unit.note: !JHN!4~35#Note:What were people saying?

trans-unit.source: According to Exegetical Helps this question was rhetorical, since they knew that Nicodemus was not from Galilee. They were angry at him for apparently siding with the despised Galilean. To accuse someone of being a Galilean was a term of the highest reproach.

trans-unit.note: !JHN!7~52#Answer:What did the Pharisees tell Nicodemus he would discover, if he looked into the matter?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!7~52#Note:What did the Pharisees tell Nicodemus he would discover, if he looked into the matter?-1173703700
trans-unit.source: According to The New International Commentary on the New Testament, the Pharisees were angry men at this point and were not thinking clearly. They overlooked Jonah, who was a Galilean, and other prophets who may have come from Galilee.

group.id: Q:JHN 8.6+Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?

trans-unit.id: q:!JHN!8~6#Question:Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?
trans-unit.source: Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?
trans-unit.note: !JHN!8~6#Question:Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?

trans-unit.id: n:!JHN!8~6#Note:Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?126779566
trans-unit.source: There is no certain answer to this. Some possible answers could be: This indicated that he did not want to pass judgment. It showed that he was embarrassed. It showed that he was considering his answer. It showed that he was acting the part of a Roman judge who was recording his answer before announcing it. It indicated contempt for the accusers. He wrote passages from the law to support his verdict, or he wrote the sins of the accusers to shame them.

group.id: Q:JUD 1.1+Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.source: Who do you think God is?
trans-unit.note: !JUD!1~1#Question:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: a:!JUD!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?1014921725
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "g" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
trans-unit.note: !JUD!1~1#Answer:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.id: n:!JUD!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?-1713399034
trans-unit.source: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralised. (Or, if it can be pluralised, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)
trans-unit.note: !JUD!1~1#Note:Who do you think God is?

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The general meaning of the Greek word apostolos is "envoy", "appointed representative", "someone who is sent on a mission". In the New Testament it develops the specific sense of an appointed representative of Jesus Christ. In Acts and the rest of the New Testament, the term "apostle" is the most common term that is used to refer to those who were commissioned by Jesus Christ to be founders of the church, and who then took up that function and position.

group.id: Q:LUK 1.1+Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?

trans-unit.source: Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?
trans-unit.target: Watu wengi walikuwa wameandika kuhusu mambo yale yale. Mambo hayo yalikuwa nini?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~1#Question:Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~1#Answer:Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?1090382148
trans-unit.source: They had been writing about the events that had taken place among them. (1)
trans-unit.target: Walikuwa wameandika kuhusu matukio yaliyotukia miongoni mwao. (1)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~1#Answer:Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~1#Note:Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?566731095
trans-unit.source: Luke used the words "among us". If your language uses one pronoun to include the listener within the group and another pronoun to exclude the listener, the pronoun used here should exclude Theophilus. The events happened among people whom Luke knew. They were groups of Jews and others who believed in Jesus. We do not know whether Theophilus was either a Jew or a believer when Luke wrote to him.
trans-unit.target: Luka alitumia maneno "katika sisi". Ikiwa lugha yako inatumia kiwakilishi kimoja kumhusisha msikilizaji ndani ya kikundi na kiwakilishi kingine kumtenga msikilizaji, kiwakilishi kilichotumiwa hapa kinapaswa kumtenga Theofilo. Matukio hayo yalitokea kati ya watu ambao Luka alijua. Walikuwa vikundi vya Wayahudi na wengine ambao walimwamini Yesu. Hatujui ikiwa Theofilo alikuwa Myahudi au mwamini wakati Luka alipomwandikia.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~1#Note:Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?

trans-unit.id: h:!LUK!1~5#Section Heading
trans-unit.source: Luke 1:5-25 An angel told Zechariah that his wife would bear his son, John the Baptizer.
trans-unit.target: Luka 1:5-25 Malaika alimwambia Zekaria kwamba mke wake angepata mwana, Yohana Mbatizaji.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Section Heading

group.id: Q:LUK 1.5-25+Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~5#Question:Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.
trans-unit.source: Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.
trans-unit.target: Niambie kuhusu mambo yaliyompata Zekaria.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Question:Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~5#Answer:Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.1859240340
trans-unit.source: An angel appeared to Zechariah while he was working in the temple as a priest. The angel told him that his wife, Elizabeth, would have a baby son and that he must name him John. Because Zechariah and Elizabeth were very old and she had never been able to have a baby before, Zechariah did not believe the angel. Because he did not believe, the angel made him unable to speak until the baby was born. After Zechariah returned home, Elizabeth became pregnant.
trans-unit.target: Wakati Zekaria alipokuwa akihudumu katika hekalu, malaika alimtokea na kumwambia kwamba mke wake, Elisabeti, angepata mtoto wa kiume na kumwita jina lake Yohana. Kwa sababu Zekaria na Elisabeti walikuwa wazee sana na hakuwa na uwezo wa kupata mtoto, Zekaria hakuamini malaika huyo. Kwa sababu ya kutoamini kwake, malaika alimfanya asiweze kusema mpaka mtoto alipozaliwa. Baada ya kurudi nyumbani, Elisabeti alipata mimba.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Answer:Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.

group.id: Q:LUK 1.5-25+What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~5#Question:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?
trans-unit.source: What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?
trans-unit.target: Ni nini kilichokuwa muhimu sana kuhusu Elisabeti kupata mimba na kuzaa mwana hivi kwamba Luka alimwandikia Theofilo kuhusu jambo hilo?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Question:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~5#Answer:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?-59396525
trans-unit.source: An old, barren couple conceiving and bearing a child (7) would show that God was doing this. People would know that God had important work for John to do when he grew up (15-17).
trans-unit.target: Wenzi wa ndoa wazee, wasiozaa wanaopata mimba na kuzaa mtoto (7) wangeonyesha kwamba Mungu alikuwa akifanya hivyo. Watu wangejua kwamba Mungu alikuwa na kazi muhimu ya Yohana kufanya alipokuwa mtu mzima (15-17).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Answer:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~5#Answer:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?-1329654652
trans-unit.source: John would prepare people for Jesus's coming (17).
trans-unit.target: Yohana angewatayarisha watu kwa ajili ya kuja kwa Yesu (17).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~5#Answer:What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?

trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The word "lord" refers to a person who has authority over another person. God has supernatural authority over all of mankind because he created everyone and everything in the world. See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~10#Answer:Where were they praying?722374153
trans-unit.source: They were outside (the temple building, but not outside the temple grounds). (10)

group.id: Q:LUK 1.11-13+What do you think an altar is?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~11#Question:What do you think an altar is?
trans-unit.source: What do you think an altar is?
trans-unit.target: Unafikiri madhabahu ni nini?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Question:What do you think an altar is?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~11#Answer:What do you think an altar is?9832483
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: It is a table-like structure usually made of wood or piled stones. Gifts of incense, food, animals or other valuable things are set on its flat top to give to God or to other spirits. Often those gifts are burned up on the top of the altar. The altar of incense in the temple was made of wood and then covered with gold (Exod. 30:1-10; 37:25-29; 1 Chron. 28:18).
trans-unit.target: Neno Muhimu: Ni jengo kama meza ambalo kwa kawaida lilitengenezwa kwa mbao au mawe yaliyowekwa kwa wingi. Zawadi za uvumba, chakula, wanyama au vitu vingine vya thamani huwekwa juu ya juu yake gorofa ili kutoa kwa Mungu au kwa roho wengine. Mara nyingi zawadi hizo huchomwa juu ya madhabahu. Madhabahu ya uvumba katika hekalu ilifanywa kwa mbao na kisha kufunikwa kwa dhahabu (Kutoka 30:1-10; 37:25-29; 1 Nyakati 28:18).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Answer:What do you think an altar is?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~11#Note:What do you think an altar is?1096164273
trans-unit.source: See "altar" in KBT.
trans-unit.target: Ona "madhabahu" katika KBT.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Note:What do you think an altar is?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~11#Answer:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.340958699
trans-unit.source: (Because many languages describe "right" and "left" by referring to a person's or animal's "hands", an object like an altar cannot have a "right side" or a "left side", even though the Greek and English languages allow it. The object that the person is using to represent the altar should be at that person's left side as he/she faces you, the checker.
trans-unit.target: (Kwa sababu lugha nyingi zinaelezea "kulia" na "kushoto" kwa kurejelea "mikono" ya mtu au mnyama, kitu kama madhabahu hakiwezi kuwa na "upande wa kulia" au "upande wa kushoto", hata ingawa lugha za Kigiriki na Kiingereza huruhusu. Kitu ambacho mtu anatumia kuwakilisha madhabahu kinapaswa kuwa upande wa kushoto wa mtu huyo wakati anakuangalia, checker.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Answer:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~11#Answer:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.-255819187
trans-unit.source: If the person is not standing in the correct place, you should go and stand in the correct position. Then ask the person to tell you the correct way to describe where you are now standing. That may be by saying that the altar was at the angel's left-hand side.)
trans-unit.target: Ikiwa mtu huyo hajasimama mahali panapofaa, unapaswa kwenda na kusimama mahali panapofaa. Kisha umwombe mtu huyo akueleze njia sahihi ya kuelezea mahali unaposimama sasa. Hiyo inaweza kuwa kwa kusema kwamba madhabahu ilikuwa upande wa kushoto wa malaika.)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Answer:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~11#Note:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.-146887127
trans-unit.source: A few writers say that the "right side" referred to Zechariah's right side, but the grammar here parallels other examples that are not disputed, such as Mark 10:37 and John 21:6.
trans-unit.target: Waandishi wachache husema kwamba "upande wa kuume" ulirejezea upande wa kuume wa Zekaria, lakini sarufi hapa inalingana na vielelezo vingine visivyopingwa, kama vile Marko 10:37 na Yohana 21:6.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~11#Note:Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.

trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~12#Question:How did Zechariah feel when he saw the angel?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~12#Answer:How did Zechariah feel when he saw the angel?1185558238

trans-unit.target: Aliogopa na kuogopa. (12)

group.id: Q:LUK 1.13+What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~13#Question:What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?
trans-unit.source: What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?
trans-unit.target: Malaika alimwambia Zekaria nini kuhusu hilo?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Question:What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~13#Answer:What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?-1783144649
trans-unit.source: Zechariah should not be afraid because God had heard [and was ready to answer] his prayer (about having a son). (13)
trans-unit.target: Zakariya hapaswi kuogopa kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa amesikia [na alikuwa tayari kujibu] maombi yake (ya kuwa na mwana). (13)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Answer:What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.13+What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~13#Question:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?
trans-unit.source: What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?
trans-unit.target: Malaika alisema nini kingine kuhusu Mungu kujibu sala ya Zekaria?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Question:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~13#Answer:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?-1919169484
trans-unit.source: Zechariah's wife, Elizabeth, would give birth to his son and he must name the boy John. (13)
trans-unit.target: Mke wa Zekaria, Elisabeti, atazaa mwana, naye anapaswa kumwita jina Yohana. (13)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Answer:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~13#Answer:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?-1789459992
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: Choosing the right name for a person or a place was extremely important to the Jews. See "name" in KBT.
trans-unit.target: Kuchunguza Maneno Muhimu: Wayahudi waliona ni muhimu sana kuchagua jina linalofaa la mtu au mahali.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Answer:What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.15-17+How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~15#Question:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?
trans-unit.source: How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?
trans-unit.target: Maisha ya Yohana yangethibitishaje kwamba alikuwa mfanyakazi wa Mungu mwenye thamani?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Question:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?1956334743
trans-unit.source: He would never drink wine or any other drink that could make him drunk. (15)
trans-unit.target: Hangeweza kamwe kunywa divai au kinywaji kingine chochote ambacho kingeweza kumfanya alewe. (15)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?1140068998
trans-unit.source: He would be filled with the Holy Spirit right from his birth or even before that. // He would have the Holy Spirit in his life right from his birth or even before that. (15)
trans-unit.target: Yeye atakuwa amejazwa na Roho Mtakatifu mara tu baada ya kuzaliwa kwake au hata kabla ya hapo. // Yeye atakuwa na Roho Mtakatifu katika maisha yake mara tu baada ya kuzaliwa kwake au hata kabla ya hapo. (15)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?-1681579713
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: The Holy Spirit is the spirit of the holy God. He works in people's hearts/spirits/lives on God's behalf, revealing God's will to us and guiding us to please God. See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "advocate, counselor" entry and also in the "spirit" entry.
trans-unit.target: Angalia neno muhimu: Roho Mtakatifu ni roho ya Mungu mtakatifu. Yeye hufanya kazi katika mioyo ya watu/roho/maisha kwa niaba ya Mungu, akifunua mapenzi ya Mungu kwetu na kutuongoza kumpendeza Mungu. Angalia "Roho Mtakatifu" katika KBT katika "mwanasheria, mshauri" kuingia na pia katika "roho" kuingia.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?683300908
trans-unit.source: He would cause many Israelites/Jews to turn [their hearts/lives away from sin] to obeying God. (16)
trans-unit.target: Angesababisha Waisraeli/Wayahudi wengi kugeuza [mioyo/maisha yao kutoka kwa dhambi] kumtii Mungu. (16)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?1150265162
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: See "Israel" and "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel, Jew, Hebrew" entry.
trans-unit.target: Angalia neno muhimu: Tazama "Israeli" na "Myahudi" katika KBT katika "Israeli, Myahudi, Kiebrania" kuingia.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?1840292929
trans-unit.source: He would work with the same kind of power and spirit as [the prophet] Elijah had done. (17)
trans-unit.target: Angetenda kwa aina ile ile ya nguvu na roho kama [nabii] Eliya alivyofanya. (17)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~15#Answer:How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.14-17+Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~14#Question:Who do you think Elijah was?
trans-unit.source: Who do you think Elijah was?
trans-unit.target: Unafikiri Eliya alikuwa nani?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Question:Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?863724745
trans-unit.source: He was a prophet in Old Testament times (1Kng. 17-2Kng. 2).
trans-unit.target: Alikuwa nabii katika nyakati za Agano la Kale (1Wafalme 17-2Wafalme 2).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?-1501749298
trans-unit.source: He did many miracles and spoke God's messages to many people, including many kings.
trans-unit.target: Alifanya miujiza mingi na aliwaambia watu ujumbe wa Mungu, kutia ndani wafalme.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?-924059448
trans-unit.source: He never died, but God took him up to heaven alive (2Kng. 2).
trans-unit.target: Hakufa kamwe, lakini Mungu alimchukua mbinguni akiwa hai (2Wafalme 2).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Answer:Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~14#Note:Who do you think Elijah was?308012005
trans-unit.source: Luke did not use the word "prophet" here, but this question checks the respondent's understanding of who Elijah was and what he had done.
trans-unit.target: Luka hakutumia neno "nabii" hapa, lakini swali hilo linajaribu uelewaji wa yule aliyehojiwa kuhusu Eliya alikuwa nani na alichokuwa amefanya.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Note:Who do you think Elijah was?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~14#Note:Who do you think Elijah was?1504936229
trans-unit.source: You may want to make a footnote or reference that in the last two verses of the Old Testament God said that he would send Elijah back to earth just before the savior would come. More than four hundred years later the angel Gabriel used those very same words when he told Zechariah what his son John would do. Jesus later said that John had done the same work in the same way as Elijah had done earlier (see Matt. 11:14; Mark 9:11-13).
trans-unit.target: Unaweza kutaka kueleza au kueleza kwamba katika mistari miwili ya mwisho ya Agano la Kale Mungu alisema kwamba atamtuma Eliya duniani kabla tu ya mkombozi kuja. Zaidi ya miaka mia nne baadaye malaika Gabrieli alitumia maneno hayo yale yale alipomwambia Zekaria kile ambacho mwanawe Yohana angefanya. Baadaye Yesu alisema kwamba Yohana alikuwa amefanya kazi ile ile kwa njia ile ile ambayo Eliya alikuwa amefanya hapo awali (ona Mt. 11:14; Marko 9:11-13).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Note:Who do you think Elijah was?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.14-17+What do you think a prophet does?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~14#Question:What do you think a prophet does?
trans-unit.source: What do you think a prophet does?
trans-unit.target: Unafikiri nabii hufanya nini?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Question:What do you think a prophet does?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~14#Answer:What do you think a prophet does?-625562265
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: A prophet tells people messages that come from the spirit world. In the Bible only the men who spoke messages from God were called prophets. They spoke for God about what he had done in the past or would do in the future. They told how that would affect the people who were listening to them.
trans-unit.target: Katika Biblia ni watu tu waliotoa ujumbe kutoka kwa Mungu walioitwa manabii. Walizungumza kwa niaba ya Mungu kuhusu kile alichokuwa amefanya au kile ambacho angefanya wakati ujao. Waliwaambia jinsi ambavyo hilo lingekuwa na athari kwa watu waliokuwa wakisikiliza.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Answer:What do you think a prophet does?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~14#Note:What do you think a prophet does?1392056846
trans-unit.source: See "prophet" in KBT.
trans-unit.target: Ona "nabii" katika Kiswahili cha Kiingereza.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~14#Note:What do you think a prophet does?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.16-17+What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~16#Question:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?
trans-unit.source: What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?
trans-unit.target: Yohana angefanya kazi gani muhimu atakapozeeka?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~16#Question:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?663441937
trans-unit.source: He would help many Israelites/Jews to turn their hearts to God (16) by turning their hearts to [love] their fellowmen/children, and by turning away from disobeying God to following the way of people who acted rightly. (17),
trans-unit.target: Angesaidia Waisraeli/Wayahudi wengi kugeuza mioyo yao kwa Mungu (16) kwa kugeuza mioyo yao kwa [upendo] kwa wenzao/watoto wao, na kwa kugeuka mbali na kutomtii Mungu na kufuata njia ya watu waliofanya haki (17),
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?866551347
trans-unit.source: -OR-
trans-unit.target: - AU -
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?11342919
trans-unit.source: He would go ahead of the Lord (their God) and get many people ready for him to come into their lives (physically and spiritually/to rule and reign).
trans-unit.target: Angetangulia mbele ya Bwana (Mungu wao) na kuwafanya watu wengi wawe tayari kwa yeye kuja katika maisha yao (kwa mwili na kiroho / kutawala na kutawala).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~16#Answer:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~16#Note:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?-1202591189
trans-unit.source: The words "the Lord" as found here in some English translations is the word "him" in the Greek text. "Him" clearly refers back five words earlier to "the Lord their God" (vs. 16). The Jews referred to only one spirit being as "the Lord" (see Deut. 6, especially vs. 4). Any words used in a translation that only allow for Jesus, the Messiah, to be understood in this verse need adjusting.
trans-unit.target: Maneno "Bwana" kama yanavyopatikana hapa katika tafsiri fulani za Kiingereza ni neno "yeye" katika maandishi ya Kigiriki. "Yeye" kwa wazi inahusu maneno matano mapema kwa "Bwana Mungu wao" (mstari wa 16). Wayahudi walitaja tu roho moja kuwa "Bwana" (tazama Kumbukumbu la Torati 6, hasa mstari wa 4).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~16#Note:What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.14-17+What do you think a righteous person is like?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~14#Question:What do you think a righteous person is like?
trans-unit.source: What do you think a righteous person is like?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.13+What was the angel's good news?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~13#Question:What was the angel's good news?
trans-unit.source: What was the angel's good news?
trans-unit.target: Malaika huyo alitoa habari gani njema?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Question:What was the angel's good news?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~13#Answer:What was the angel's good news?-557174445
trans-unit.source: God had heard Zechariah's prayers to have a child. He was going to give Zechariah a son (13).
trans-unit.target: Mungu alikuwa amesikia sala za Zekaria za kuomba mtoto. Mungu angempa Zekaria mwana (13).
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Answer:What was the angel's good news?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~13#Note:What was the angel's good news?838484588
trans-unit.source: The Greek word Luke used here means "tell good news". It is the same word he used regularly elsewhere in this book to indicate that God's plan to send the Messiah to save people was happening right then. That meaning is also in the words of the angel here (17), but it is not what a person would think of immediately. Zechariah's son would be preparing people for the Lord God's coming into the world in the person of his son, Jesus, to save them. That was "good news". If the respondent includes this point in his/her answer, give him/her special praise.
trans-unit.target: Neno la Kigiriki ambalo Luka alitumia hapa linamaanisha "kuhubiri habari njema". Ni neno lile lile alilotumia mara kwa mara mahali pengine katika kitabu hiki kuonyesha kwamba mpango wa Mungu wa kumtuma Masihi kuwaokoa watu ulikuwa unatokea wakati huo. Maana hiyo pia iko katika maneno ya malaika hapa (17), lakini sio kile mtu angefikiria mara moja. Mwana wa Zekaria angekuwa akiwatayarisha watu kwa kuja kwa Bwana Mungu ulimwenguni katika mtu wa mwanawe, Yesu, kuwaokoa. Hiyo ilikuwa "habari njema". Ikiwa mjibu anajumuisha jambo hili katika jibu lake, mpe sifa maalum.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~13#Note:What was the angel's good news?

trans-unit.source: Luke 1:26-38 An angel told Mary that she would bear God's son, Jesus.
trans-unit.target: Luka 1:26-38 Malaika alimwambia Maria kwamba angemzaa Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~26#Section Heading

group.id: Q:LUK 1.26-38+Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~26#Question:Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.
trans-unit.source: Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.
trans-unit.target: Niambie kuhusu mambo yaliyompata Mary.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~26#Question:Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~26#Answer:Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.-759961226
trans-unit.source: God sent an angel to tell Mary that she would have a baby son and that his name would be Jesus. Mary was surprised and frightened by this. She asked the angel how this could happen because she was not married yet. The angel said that God himself would cause her to become pregnant. Therefore, the child would be the son of God. Mary accepted that this was what God wanted for her, so she was willing for this to happen to her.
trans-unit.target: Malaika alitumwa na Bwana kumwambia Mariamu kwamba atazaa mtoto na kwamba jina lake litakuwa Yesu. Mariamu alishangaa na kuogopa. Alimwuliza malaika jinsi hii inaweza kuwa kwani alikuwa bado hajaoa. Malaika alisema kwamba Bwana mwenyewe atamfanya awe na mimba na kwa hivyo mtoto huyo atakuwa mwana wa Mungu. Mariamu aliamini kwamba hii ilikuwa mapenzi ya Mungu kwake, kwa hivyo alitaka hii ifanyike kwake.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~26#Answer:Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?-1858722496

trans-unit.target: Yesu angefanya kazi muhimu kwa ajili ya Mungu, na watu/Mungu wangemwita Mwana wa Aliye Juu/Mungu Aliye Juu. (32)

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?1540614940
trans-unit.source: The Lord [who is] God would make him a king, as his ancestor David had been. (32)
trans-unit.target: Bwana Mungu atamtawaza kuwa mfalme, kama Daudi baba yake.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?866551347
trans-unit.source: -OR-
trans-unit.target: - AU -
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?-453608866

trans-unit.target: Bwana [ambaye ni] Mungu atampa mamlaka ya kutawala kama babu yake [Mfalme] Daudi alivyofanya. (32)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?-380209787
trans-unit.source: Jesus's reign over the descendants of Jacob [Israel/God's people] would never end. (33)
trans-unit.target: Utawala wa Yesu juu ya wazao wa Yakobo [Israeli/watu wa Mungu] haungekoma kamwe. (33)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~31#Answer:What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.34+After hearing that she would bear a child, what did Mary ask?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.35+What did the angel say would show that it was true that God made it happen?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~35#Answer:What did the angel say would show that it was true that God made it happen?1404800344
trans-unit.source: The child would be holy and would be called the son of God. (35)

group.id: Q:LUK 1.34-37+What do you think makes someone holy?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~34#Question:What do you think makes someone holy?
trans-unit.source: What do you think makes someone holy?
trans-unit.target: Unafikiri ni nini humfanya mtu awe mtakatifu?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~34#Question:What do you think makes someone holy?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~34#Answer:What do you think makes someone holy?-565022241
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: God declares that person to be set apart from the way people live to please themselves. He sets them apart in order to totally serve him. That person would be morally pure, acting in all ways like God would act.
trans-unit.target: Mungu anamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa ametengwa na njia ya watu ya kuishi ili kujipendeza mwenyewe. Anawatenga ili wamtumikie yeye kabisa. Mtu huyo atakuwa safi kiadili, akitenda katika njia zote kama Mungu atakavyofanya.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~34#Answer:What do you think makes someone holy?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~34#Note:What do you think makes someone holy?381911298
trans-unit.source: If you discuss how God is holy, see the question at verses 49b-50 below.
trans-unit.target: Ikiwa unazungumzia jinsi Mungu alivyo mtakatifu, ona swali kwenye mstari wa 49b-50 hapa chini.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~34#Note:What do you think makes someone holy?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.36-37+Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~36#Question:Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?
trans-unit.source: Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?
trans-unit.target: Kwa nini malaika alimwambia Maria kwamba Elisabeti alikuwa na mimba?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~36#Question:Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~36#Answer:Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?-1336681809
trans-unit.source: Elizabeth, who had been unable to have children and now was very old, was already into her sixth month of pregnancy. Since that seemed impossible, but was true, then nothing would be too difficult for God to do. [Mary, too, would have the baby the angel was telling her about.] // Whatever God says will happen, he will use his great power to make happen. He had already helped old Elizabeth become pregnant. [Therefore, Mary should believe what the angel was telling her also.] (36-37)
trans-unit.target: Elisabeti, ambaye alikuwa tasa na sasa alikuwa mzee sana, alikuwa tayari katika mwezi wake wa sita wa ujauzito. Kwa kuwa hilo lilionekana kuwa lisilowezekana, lakini lilikuwa kweli, basi hakuna kitu ambacho kingekuwa ngumu sana kwa Mungu kufanya. [Maria, pia, angekuwa na mtoto ambaye malaika alikuwa akimwambia.] // Chochote Mungu anasema kitatokea, atatumia nguvu yake kuu kufanya iwe hivyo. Alikuwa tayari amemsaidia Elisabeti mzee kupata mimba. [Kwa hivyo, Maria anapaswa kuamini kile malaika alikuwa akimwambia pia.] (36-37)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~36#Answer:Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.38+When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~38#Question:When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?
trans-unit.source: When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?
trans-unit.target: Mwanzoni, Zekaria hakuamini kwamba jambo alilosema malaika lingetukia.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Question:When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~38#Answer:When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?1677568203
trans-unit.source: She did believe him.
trans-unit.target: Alimwamini.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Answer:When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.38+What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~38#Question:What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?
trans-unit.source: What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?
trans-unit.target: Maria alisema nini ili kuonyesha kwamba alimwamini Yesu?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Question:What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~38#Answer:What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?-630726913
trans-unit.source: She said that she was ready to serve God, to allow him to use her in the way the angel had said. // Because she thought of herself as God's servant/slave, she would be happy for him to use her in the way the angel had said.
trans-unit.target: Alisema kwamba alikuwa tayari kumtumikia Mungu, kumruhusu amtumie kwa njia ambayo malaika alikuwa amesema. // Kwa sababu alijiona kuwa mtumishi / mtumwa wa Mungu, angekuwa na furaha kwake kumtumia kwa njia ambayo malaika alikuwa amesema.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Answer:What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.38+What do you think a slave is?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~38#Question:What do you think a slave is?
trans-unit.source: What do you think a slave is?
trans-unit.target: Unafikiri mtumwa ni nani?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Question:What do you think a slave is?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~38#Answer:What do you think a slave is?450734104
trans-unit.source: Key Term Check: A slave is a person who must do whatever his/her master wants because the master owns the person as a possession. The slave is not free to do what he likes or go where he likes.
trans-unit.target: Mtumwa ni mtu ambaye lazima afanye chochote bwana wake anachotaka kwa sababu bwana anamiliki mtu huyo kama mali. Mtumwa hana uhuru wa kufanya anachotaka au kwenda mahali anapopenda.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Answer:What do you think a slave is?

trans-unit.id: n:!LUK!1~38#Note:What do you think a slave is?-1517934172
trans-unit.source: See "servant, slave" in KBT.
trans-unit.target: Ona "mtumwa, mtumwa" katika KBT.
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~38#Note:What do you think a slave is?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.39-45+When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~39#Question:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?
trans-unit.source: When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?
trans-unit.target: Mariamu alipomtembelea Elisabeti, ni jambo gani lililotukia lililoonyesha kwamba Mungu alikuwa pamoja na wanawake hao wawili?
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~39#Question:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?645965034
trans-unit.source: The Holy Spirit filled/inspired/caused Elizabeth to speak like a prophet about Mary and the child she would bear. (41-42)
trans-unit.target: Roho Mtakatifu alijaza/aliongoza/alifanya Elisabeti kusema kama nabii kuhusu Mariamu na mtoto ambaye angezaa (41-42)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?866551347
trans-unit.source: -OR-
trans-unit.target: - AU -
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?209139337
trans-unit.source: Before Mary said anything more than a greeting to Elizabeth, God's Spirit had already revealed to Elizabeth what was happening to Mary and that Mary had believed that it would happen. (41-45)
trans-unit.target: Kabla ya Mariamu kusema chochote zaidi ya salamu kwa Elisabeti, Roho wa Mungu alikuwa tayari amemfunulia Elisabeti kile kilichokuwa kikimpata Mariamu na kwamba Mariamu alikuwa ameamini kwamba kitatokea. (41-45)
trans-unit.note: !LUK!1~39#Answer:When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?

group.id: Q:LUK 1.39+What did Mary do in the days following the angel's visit to her?

trans-unit.id: q:!LUK!1~39#Question:What did Mary do in the days following the angel's visit to her?
trans-unit.source: What did Mary do in the days following the angel's visit to her?
trans-unit.target: Maria alifanya nini katika siku zilizofuata ziara ya malaika?

trans-unit.id: a:!LUK!1~39#Answer:What did Mary do in the days following the angel's visit to her?-238315625
trans-unit.source: She got ready and went quickly to the town where Elizabeth lived. (39)
trans-unit.target: Akaondoka akaenda upesi kwenye mji ambako Elisabeti aliishi. (39)
